elements.evidence: "for the use of Sparkling, affiliated companies of Sparkling"

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf

elements.evidence: Grant remains "a non-exclusive licence ... to use" with no perpetual term stated anywhere in the redline.
No irrevocability language added; only "non-transferable" was struck and a successor-transfer right inserted.

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: No termination-trigger limitation appears; the redline touches only the grant scope and assignment provisions.
"transferable to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Sparkling's assets"
"affiliated companies of Sparkling" are covered in the grant with no notice condition (better than fallback).

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "except that either party may assign this Agreement to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets without such consent"

offending_extra_words: in each case at the Authorized Locations
except as permitted by Section 2 or Section 20(d) or
except that either party may assign this Agreement to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets without such consent.
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the redline delivers only the fallback bargain: affiliate and contractor coverage plus successor transfer, with no perpetual/irrevocable language for paid-up licences and no limitation of subscription termination to uncured material breach.
Perpetuity and irrevocability are distinct atomic elements and each fails independently; nothing in the operative text supplies either, and the margin comment does not cure the omission.

Minimality fails: operation 1 rewrites the whole grant preamble (21 words to 47, changed-character ratio 0.606) when a targeted deletion of "non-transferable" plus a short contractor/successor insertion would suffice; the added "in each case at the Authorized Locations" restructures the original affiliate location qualifier unnecessarily.
Operation 3 expands 8 words to 38 (ratio 4.75) and duplicates the successor-transfer right already granted in the licence clause, creating overlapping protection rather than a single tight edit.

Operation 2's cross-references to "Section 2 or Section 20(d)" add bespoke numbering not otherwise relied upon in the edited text; a generic "except as otherwise permitted by this Agreement" would have been tighter.

Untouched commercial terms (Authorized Locations fee mechanic, object-code restriction, documentation licence) remain effective and no undefined term or contradiction is introduced, so intent is preserved.
